data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Practise degree modifiers and intensifiers such as highly, deeply, absolutely, fairly, rather and slightly.
learningPoints: Use gradable and non-gradable adjectives with appropriate intensifiers.
Use very, fairly, rather and slightly with gradable adjectives.
Use absolutely, completely and totally with many non-gradable adjectives.
Recognise common collocations such as highly successful and deeply concerned.
Use modifiers to express fine differences in degree.
Avoid unnatural combinations such as 'very impossible'.

sections.explain: VERY naturally modifies many gradable adjectives.

words.word: The exam was very difficult.
The exam was absolutely difficult, as the neutral default for a gradable adjective.
The exam was very impossible.

sections.explain: ABSOLUTELY commonly modifies strong non-gradable adjectives such as EXHAUSTED or IMPOSSIBLE.

words.word: I was absolutely exhausted.
I was very exhausted, as the most natural strong collocation here.
I was slightly exhausted completely.

sections.explain: HIGHLY commonly combines with adjectives such as SUCCESSFUL, LIKELY and RECOMMENDED.

words.word: The project was highly successful.
The project was deeply successful.
The project was strongly success.

sections.explain: DEEPLY commonly modifies emotional adjectives such as CONCERNED, WORRIED and DISAPPOINTED.

words.word: We are deeply concerned about the situation.
We are highly concerned about the situation, as the most natural collocation.
We are deeply concern about the situation.

sections.explain: SLIGHTLY means to a small extent.

words.word: The second option is slightly cheaper.
The second option is absolutely cheaper.
The second option is slightly cheapest.

sections.explain: RATHER can indicate a fairly strong or unexpected degree, depending on context.

words.word: The room was rather small for four people.
The room was completely small for four people.
The room was rather smallest for four people.

sections.explain: COMPLETELY works naturally with adjectives such as WRONG, DIFFERENT and EMPTY.

words.word: Your answer is completely wrong.
Your answer is very wrongest.
Your answer is slightly completely wrong.
The instructions were fairly clear.
The instructions were absolutely clear, meaning only moderately clear.
The instructions were fairly clearest.

sections.explain: Strong non-gradable adjectives generally prefer intensifiers such as ABSOLUTELY rather than VERY.

words.word: The view was absolutely breathtaking.
The view was very breathtaking, as the most natural collocation.
The view was slightly absolutely breathtaking.

sections.explain: Some modifiers form conventional combinations with particular adjectives.

words.word: It is highly unlikely that they will agree.
It is deeply unlikely that they will agree.
It is highly unlikelihood that they will agree.
